summary: We are confirming that a Branch-and-Bound (BnB) maximum clique solver with degeneracy ordering achieves a perfect score of 100 on problem #185 (N≤1000, M≤500K), replicating the iter-2 result at full scope. A second arm tests timing robustness by halving the time budget from 1950ms to 1000ms.
key_points: h-main: BnB with degeneracy ordering, greedy coloring bound (bitset color classes), and greedy warm-starts, using a 1950ms budget. Predicted score: 100. This confirms the iter-2 winning algorithm in real mode.
h-robustness: Identical algorithm but with a 1000ms time budget. Predicted score: 100. If it drops below 100, we learn which test instances are timing-critical and how thin the safety margin is.

Confirmation criteria: h-main scoring 100 validates the algorithm for deployment. If h-main scores <100, we need to investigate dense-subgraph instances and potentially reintroduce the DLS (Dynamic Local Search) fallback from iter-1. If h-robustness also scores 100, the timing margin is comfortable (≥2× headroom).

Key design choices: degeneracy ordering (highest core number first) for early pruning, greedy coloring upper bound for branch cutting, per-vertex greedy warm-starts (top-100 by core number), and time-check every 2048 BnB calls to stay within budget.
